dialogue.content: Set the camera so that the brightest part of the speckle pattern uses most of the camera's range without saturating, and report the exposure and gain you chose.

Decision 1/10 -> hardware
Instruction: Tune the camera so the brightest part of the speckle pattern uses most of the dynamic range without saturating. Steps: 1) Read current settings (exposure, gain, bit depth, max pixel value). 2) Set gain to its minimum (or lowest sensible) value. 3) Capture a frame, and report the max pixel value and the number of saturated pixels. 4) Adjust exposure iteratively (scale by target/measured max) until the frame max is about 85-95% of the full-scale value (e.g. ~3500-3900 of 4095 for 12-bit, or ~230-243 of 255 for 8-bit) with zero saturated pixels. Only raise gain if the exposure hits its limit. 5) Save the final frame as a .npy file and report the final exposure, gain, max pixel value, saturated pixel count, and full-scale value, using only values the camera returned.
Reason: The camera must be driven to set exposure and gain and measure the peak pixel value.
